concepts.title: Hardy-Ramanujan Numbers
concepts.definition: A positive integer that can be expressed as the sum of two cubes in two different ways is known as a Hardy-Ramanujan number.
concepts.key_idea: The smallest Hardy-Ramanujan number is 1729, which equals 1^3 + 12^3 and 9^3 + 10^3.

concepts.key_idea: Multiplying a natural number three times as a factor yields its perfect cube.

concepts.title: One's Digit of a Cube
concepts.definition: The unit digit of the cube of any integer is determined solely by the unit digit of the base number.
concepts.key_idea: Cubing the last digit of a number gives the last digit of its cube.

concepts.title: Cube as Sum of Consecutive Odd Numbers
concepts.definition: The cube of any natural number n can be represented as the sum of n consecutive odd integers.
concepts.key_idea: Summing n consecutive odd numbers starting from n*(n-1)+1 yields n^3.

concepts.title: Difference of Consecutive Cubes Pattern
concepts.definition: The difference between the cubes of two consecutive natural numbers n and (n-1) follows a linear combination pattern.
concepts.key_idea: The subtraction of (n-1)^3 from n^3 equals 1 plus three times the product of n and (n-1).

concepts.title: Smallest Multiplier for Perfect Cube
concepts.definition: The minimum positive integer required to multiply a number so that every prime factor forms groups of three.
concepts.key_idea: Multiply by missing prime factors to complete every incomplete triplet in factorisation.

concepts.title: Smallest Divisor for Perfect Cube
concepts.definition: The smallest natural number by which a non-cube must be divided to eliminate prime factors that do not form complete triplets.
concepts.key_idea: Divide out all prime factors that fail to form a triplet to leave a perfect cube quotient.

concepts.title: Number of Cuboids to Form a Cube
concepts.definition: The total count of identical cuboids of given side lengths needed to assemble a solid perfect cube.
concepts.key_idea: Divide the target cube volume by the cuboid volume to find the number of cuboids required.

concepts.title: Cube Root by Prime Factorisation
concepts.definition: Determining the number whose cube equals a given integer by selecting one prime factor from each group of three identical factors.
concepts.key_idea: Group prime factors into triplets and multiply one representative factor from each triplet.
